content_sections.heading: About the Institute
content_sections.text: The notice describes WII as an autonomous institution under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), Government of India, which offers training programmes, academic courses and advisory in wildlife research and management. Its Recruitment and Placement Cell is at Chandrabani, Dehradun, Uttarakhand-248002. The positions are for research projects and the notice states that they are temporary for the project period.

content_sections.heading: Vacancy Details
content_sections.text: The notice invites applications for 26 positions in total across nine projects. The break-up below adds up to 26 (5 + 1 + 2 + 1 + 4 + 1 + 1 + 6 + 5). The notice prints no category-wise break-up. Project 01: Conservation and Management of the critically endangered gharial (Gavialis gangeticus) Project 02: Reviving Batagur baska: A Strategic Conservation Approach for Ensuring Survival of the Critically Endangered Terrapins Project 03: Impact Assessment of Vibrations on Aquatic Life and Biodiversity Due to Underwater Tunnel Construction Under River Brahmaputra Project 04: Rangewide Estimation of Riverine and Estuarine Dolphin in India- 2nd cycle Project 05: Preparation of a site-specific wildlife management plan to mitigate the ecological impacts of proposed forest land diversion for mining in Bonai Forest Division, Sundargarh, Odisha Project 06: Conservation Advisory and Policy Cell Project 07: Assessing population dynamics, genetics and breeding patterns of threatened mountain ungulates for species recovery and community-based conservation in the Western Himalayas Project 08: Project Great Indian Bustard Project 09: CAMPA Dugong Recovery Programme

content_sections.heading: Who Can Apply
content_sections.text: Only Indian nationals may apply. Qualification, experience and desirable requirements differ by position and are given below as the notice prints them. The age limits are in the table above; the notice prints no "as on" date for counting age. Relaxation in the upper age limit applies as per the Government of India, Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions (Department of Personnel & Training) OM No. 15012/2/2010- Estt. (D) dated 27.03.2012, as amended from time to time. As of now: Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes up to 5 years; Other Backward Class (OBC) up to 3 years. Essential: Four Years Bachelor's Degree (4 Yr. BSc degree as per National Education Policy) in Natural Sciences (Wildlife Science/ Zoology/ Ecology/ Marine Sciences/ Marine Biology/ Environmental Sciences/ Geoinformatics/ Life Sciences)/ Agricultural/ Forestry Sciences from recognized institute/ University AND four years of experience (after obtaining four years' degree) in R&D in Industrials or Science & Technology Institutions or Scientific activities and Services. OR Master's Degree in Natural Sciences (same subjects)/ Agricultural Sciences from recognized institute/ University AND four years of experience (after obtaining Master's degree) in R&D in Industrials or Science & Technology Institutions or Scientific activities and Services. Desirable: work experience in riverine ecology and Gangetic River system, with expertise in Gharial and other crocodilians, including population surveys, nesting ecology, habitat assessment and field-based research. Proficiency in GIS, statistical analysis, Genetic studies, camera trapping, community engagement, human–wildlife conflict mitigation, project coordination and scientific report writing is desirable. Preference will be given to candidates with a Ph.D. in a relevant discipline. Essential: Four Years Bachelor's Degree (4 Years BSc degree as per National Education Policy) in Natural Sciences (Wildlife Science/ Zoology/ Ecology/ Marine Science/ Marine Biology/ Environmental Sciences/ Geoinformatics/ Life Science)/ Agricultural Sciences from recognised institute/ University AND two years of experience (after obtaining four years' degree) in R&D in Industrials of Science & Technology Institutions or Scientific activities and services. OR Master's Degree in Natural Science (same subjects)/ Agricultural Sciences AND two years of experience (after obtaining Master's degree) in the same. Desirable: experience in field-based research in crocodilian biology, Gangetic River ecology, or aquatic wildlife conservation. Candidates with skills in boat-based river surveys, nest monitoring, telemetry, Genetic studies, GIS, camera trapping and ecological statistics/data analysis with a keen interest in extensive field-based research in different landscapes of India will be preferred. content_sections.heading: Pay and Tenure
content_sections.text: Pay is printed as monthly emoluments, with HRA shown as "+ HRA" for every post except the Project Manager, whose emoluments are printed as 60,000 to 1,25,000 and fixed depending on experience. Most Project Associate positions carry two pay figures, one for NET/GATE qualified candidates and one for non-NET/GATE candidates, exactly as in the vacancy table. For Project Associate – I in Projects 01 and 09 the notice prints the lower figure (30,000 + HRA) against NET/GATE candidates and the higher figure (37,000 + HRA) against non-NET/GATE candidates. The advertised positions are purely temporary for the project period and will stand abolished after the project is completed. The Institute's rules and regulations govern the project's tenure and the code of conduct of selected candidates. Candidates not found suitable for a post may be considered for a position at a lower grade on the Interview Committee's recommendation, with approval of the competent authority.

content_sections.heading: WII Recruitment 2026 Job Description
content_sections.text: The notice prints the description of work for each position as follows.

rows.duties: Field work, coordinating with Forest Department officials, supervising data collection and analysis, quality control and timely project reports under the Project Investigator's guidance, managing the team and stakeholders. Skills in boat-based river surveys, nest monitoring, telemetry, Genetic studies, GIS, camera trapping and ecological statistics/data analysis will be preferred.
Work with a team mandated to carry out field surveys, data analyses, liaisoning with forest department, report writing and all other project related works assigned by the Project Investigator.
Work with a team mandated to carry out field surveys, data analyses, liaisoning with forest department and all other project related works assigned by the Project Investigator.

Data collection on river terrapin and associated ecological parameters across remote landscapes of Sundarban, West Bengal, including report writing, visual encounter surveys, nocturnal and diurnal field patrolling, habitat assessment, monitoring activity patterns and population trends, handling and tagging for movement ecology studies, data management and analysis, sample collection for genetic studies, and community-based awareness and outreach.

The notice's description of work for this post reads: experience in integrating genetic data with ecological assessments and conducting fieldwork in remote riverine habitats with limited logistical support is desirable; research publications in peer-reviewed journals are an added advantage.
Assist in molecular biology aspects related to conservation of Gangetic dolphins and riverine ecology in general.

Conduct social surveys to assess human–wildlife interactions and conflicts, including collection and documentation of socio-economic and conflict-related data; assist in data analysis, interpretation, scientific report writing, and preparation of management and mitigation recommendations.

Conduct GIS and remote sensing analysis, including land-use/land-cover, habitat and other thematic maps; assist in spatial data processing, satellite image interpretation, field data integration, and preparation of maps and GIS-based inputs for the wildlife management plan.
Conduct field surveys and collection of data; data analysis and scientific report writing.

Primarily a managerial role overseeing all activities of the cell; assisting in developing proposals, conducting site inspections, reviewing reports and other tasks assigned by the Nodal Officer; managing competing demands and deadlines.
Laboratory research on the project: sample management and data generation, data curation, analysis, overall project coordination and report writing.
In situ, ex situ and outreach work in bustard range states.
Field research and conservation/conservation breeding of Great Indian Bustard and Lesser Florican.
Field research on threat assessment, ecological monitoring and outreach in Rajasthan.
Great Indian Bustard and Lesser Florican conservation breeding.
Dugong population estimation/survey and acoustic monitoring of Dugongs in Gulf of Mannar and Palk Bay; Andaman & Nicobar and Gujarat regions.
Prepare seagrass habitat map, create dugong suitable habitats, prepare dugong distribution map, data analysis, interpretation of results and report writing.
Conduct awareness and outreach activities for the fisherman community in Tamil Nadu; place of work is Gulf of Mannar and Palk Bay, Tamil Nadu.

content_sections.heading: Selection and Interview
content_sections.text: Applicants are first shortlisted, and the top ten (10) shortlisted candidates against each advertised project/position are called for an online interview before a duly constituted Selection Committee. The notice prints no interview date. Shortlisting is based on essential qualification, age limit, percentage of marks in Bachelor's/Master's Degree, specialization relevance in Masters, research experience and publications (papers published in journals, books, and papers presented in workshops/seminars/symposiums/conferences), as per WII rules. Meeting the minimum qualification and experience does not automatically entitle an applicant to an interview. The list of shortlisted candidates and the interview result will be uploaded in the "Latest News & Announcements" section of the Institute's website at https://wii.gov.in/news . Selected candidates must produce all original documents/certificates at the time of joining and must join immediately within the duration given in the Offer Letter.

faq.question: Q1. How many vacancies are there in WII Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: The notice invites applications for 26 project positions in total, spread over nine research projects, with the posts and numbers listed in the vacancy table above.

faq.question: Q2. What is the last date to apply for WII Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: The Online Application Close Date is 01 December 2026. The application opens on 17 November 2026.

faq.question: Q3. What is the qualification for WII project posts?
faq.answer: It differs by post. Field Worker needs a graduate degree in any discipline and Administrative Assistant a Bachelor's Degree in any discipline, Project Manager a Doctoral Degree in Natural Sciences/Agricultural/Forestry Sciences, and most other posts a degree in Natural Sciences, some with R&D experience.

faq.question: Q4. What is the age limit for WII Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: It varies by post: 40 years for Senior Project Associate, 55 years for Project Manager, 50 years for Project Assistant in Projects 07 and 08(3), and 35 years for the other posts. Relaxation is up to 5 years for SC/ST and up to 3 years for OBC.

faq.question: Q5. What is the application fee for WII Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: General category applicants pay Rs. 500/-. SC/ST/OBC/EWS and Physically Challenged candidates are exempted from that fee but pay Rs. 100/- as Application Processing Fee. The fee is non-refundable.

faq.question: Q6. How do I apply for WII Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: Apply online at https://wiirp.com/application.php or through the QR code in the notice. No printed application copy is considered, and the fee receipt must be uploaded with the form.

faq.question: Q7. What is the selection process for WII Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: Applications are shortlisted on a 50-mark scoring scheme, the top ten shortlisted candidates for each project/position are called for an online interview, and a Selection Committee conducts the process.

faq.question: Q8. What is the salary for WII project posts and is HRA paid on top?
faq.answer: Monthly emoluments range from 4,000 + HRA for Field Worker to 60,000 to 1,25,000 for Project Manager. Except for the Project Manager, the pay is printed as "+ HRA", so HRA is shown in addition to the amount.

faq.question: Q9. Can I apply for more than one position in WII Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: Yes, for a maximum of two advertised positions relevant to your education and the essential and desirable requirements. A separate online application form, supporting documents and fee are needed for each position.

faq.answer: No. The notice says the positions are purely temporary for the project period and will stand abolished after the project is completed; most projects are one year, likely to be extended.
